reviewed_equivalence: The original failure is a repository-relative versus stage-relative artifact-reference mismatch, not a scientific adequacy, model, prediction or calibration failure.

All original construction/checkpoint/invariance/source-binding checks are retained through unchanged build_evaluation_manifest, and all numeric adequacy conditions through unchanged validate_passed_adequacy.
Only artifact references are normalized in memory; each must resolve uniquely into the exact existing chr7_evaluation directory and retain its original SHA256 and byte count.
Traversal, outside-directory targets, symlink escape, duplicate aliases, missing files and hash/size drift are rejected.

The frozen release and calibration dictionaries retain identical scientific fields, six C checkpoints, seed/ensemble/inference rules, passed decision bindings and dedicated calibration inputs; added fields only reference the append-only repair note.
Synthetic absolute, stage-relative and repository-relative references yield identical scientific gate references, and failed C adequacy still blocks every path spelling.
Successful evaluation and failed original gate command records are checked; original helper, evaluation manifest and evaluation input are hashed before and after verification.
Both original gate outputs were independently confirmed absent before repair. Exclusive new writes preserve all original payloads and the failed command record.
conclusion: No blocking issue identified. This is a bounded metadata-reference repair that leaves the frozen scientific procedure and completed evaluation unchanged.
